xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3959: Record the transcript path in the session index at session start; resolver stops guessing per harness

plan.title: Record the transcript path in the session index at session start; resolver stops guessing per harness
plan.author: agent:k3

narratives.Problem: Resolving where an agent's transcript lives requires per-harness path formulas applied to session ids, duplicated across two resolver adapters (sync agent-enrichment, async jsonl-resolver) that must stay parity-perfect, plus launcher.sh greps and runtime-state mirrors that exist only because the sessions.json index never recorded the path it already knew at session start.
narratives.Proposal: Add an optional absolute `path` field to session-index entries; every harness capture point (Claude SessionStart/heartbeat hooks, codex thread capture, kimi session capture, pi/ohmypi extension session_start/turn_end, ACP host, muse spawn) appends it; both resolver adapters short-circuit per-harness formulas for path-carrying entries; then delete the launcherPinned and stateDerived guessing extras. Per-entry formula branches stay untouched as the legacy fallback (PAN-3958 consolidates them). Baseline is origin/feature/pan-3950 @ fd42eb98876 per the operator's planning note.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Consolidating or deleting the per-entry per-harness path formulas (PAN-3958)
- Touching the legacy fallback branches for pathless entries
- Instrumenting conversation-launched muse sessions (no capture point exists; they resolve via conversation routes)
- Changing watchForAgentTranscriptCandidate (it shrinks automatically as candidates become exact)
- Moving or renaming the exported resolve* helpers in jsonl-resolver.ts (ws-rpc and conversation modules import them)
- Deleting historical transcripts or rewriting existing sessions.json lines

autoDecisions.summary: Baseline is origin/feature/pan-3950 @ fd42eb98876, not main
autoDecisions.rationale: Operator planning note on the issue directs planning against the shape PR #3951 lands; the sessions.json index, orderedTranscriptCandidates, and the deleted session.id pointer all come from that branch.

autoDecisions.summary: launcherPinned + stateDerived are deleted now; per-entry formula branches are the 'legacy fallback' that stays
autoDecisions.rationale: Only reading that satisfies all three constraints: issue demands net-negative production lines and that the named tests survive deleting all harness-specific helpers except the legacy fallback; planning note demands the fallback stay untouched for PAN-3958.

autoDecisions.summary: Dedupe in parseSessionIndex inherits a displaced entry's path when the newer duplicate is pathless
autoDecisions.rationale: The server-side observeSessionIndexEvent and the jq-less hook path can append a later pathless entry for the same sessionId; plain newest-wins would erase the recorded path.

autoDecisions.summary: Pi/ohmypi record via bounded sessions-dir scan at session_start plus a turn_end sessionLogPath upgrade entry
autoDecisions.rationale: The extension's SessionStartEvent carries no path field, but TurnEndEvent.sessionLogPath is the harness's own absolute path; dedupe makes the upgraded entry authoritative.

autoDecisions.summary: Conversation-launched muse sessions are not instrumented
autoDecisions.rationale: No post-launch session wait exists on that path; adding a poller is new machinery and conversation transcripts resolve through the conversation route anyway.

autoDecisions.summary: plan.metadata.sizeJustification is set for the projected-surface lint
autoDecisions.rationale: The record shape only has value when all six harness writers land together; splitting per harness would serialize on the same schema and ship a half-instrumented index. Every file is named and each item is small.

metadata.sizeJustification: One inseparable change: the index record shape only has value when the schema (W1), the resolver fast-path (W3), and all six harness writers (W2, W4-W7) land together — splitting per harness would ship a half-instrumented index and re-create the parity drift this issue removes. Scope is already minimal: no new modules, no consolidation, ~27 named files across 9 items.

items.title: W1: Session index entries carry an optional absolute transcript path

expected_outputs: Given an appended entry carrying metadata.path, then parseSessionIndex returns the entry with path intact.
Given a pathless re-append of the same sessionId, then parseSessionIndex preserves the earlier entry's path on the kept entry.
Given an entry whose serialized line exceeds 4095 bytes, then appendSessionIdToHistory throws as before.
metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns session-history.ts and its test alone; every other item consumes the pinned record shape rather than co-editing the file (w8 shares it and is edge-gated).

narrative.Action: In src/lib/session-history.ts (baseline origin/feature/pan-3950 @ fd42eb98876): add `path?: string` to SessionIndexEntry (:30-36) with a comment that it is the absolute transcript path recorded at session start; pass it through in normalizeSessionEntry (:100-114) when it is a non-empty trimmed string; extend appendSessionIdToHistory (:205-226) metadata with `path?: string` and spread `...(path ? { path } : {})` into the serialized line (4095-byte guard unchanged); make the parseSessionIndex dedupe loop (:148-153) inherit the displaced entry's path when the newer duplicate is pathless (`!entry.path && prev?.path ? { ...entry, path: prev.path } : entry`); add one line to the module header. Extend tests/unit/lib/agents/session-index.test.ts with the round-trip, inheritance, replacement-wins, reset-clears, and oversize-throws cases from PRD W1.

items.title: Given an entry appended with metadata.path, when parseSessionIndex reads the file, then the returned entry contains the identical absolute path.
Given a path-carrying entry followed by a pathless duplicate of the same sessionId, parseSessionIndex preserves the path on the surviving entry.
Given a duplicate carrying a different path, the newer path wins outright in the parsed output.
npx vitest run tests/unit/lib/agents/session-index.test.ts exits 0 and npm run typecheck exits 0.
W2: Claude hooks and the model_set observer record transcript_path

expected_outputs: Given a SessionStart payload with transcript_path, then the appended sessions.json line contains that path and the model_set event body carries transcriptPath.
Given a model_set event with transcriptPath, then observeSessionIndexEvent appends an index entry carrying path.
metadata.parallelSafeReason: Shell hooks and one server service; no overlap with the TS writer items.

narrative.Action: pan_append_session_index in sync-sources/hooks/pan-hook-lib.sh (:121-138) gains a seventh positional arg path="${7:-}" and its jq filter becomes `{...} + (if $path == "" then {} else {path: $path} end)` with --arg path "$path". session-start-hook (:25-29, :46): parse TRANSCRIPT_PATH from .transcript_path, pass it as arg 7 to pan_append_session_index, and add transcriptPath to the model_set BODY builder (:59-61) via --arg tp + the same conditional. heartbeat-hook (:68-70): parse .transcript_path from its payload and pass it as arg 7. In src/dashboard/server/services/agent-state-service.ts observeSessionIndexEvent (:73-84), the payload type gains transcriptPath?: string and the append call passes { model: payload.model, path: payload.transcriptPath } (undefined when empty). Extend tests/scripts/session-start-hook.test.ts to assert the sessions.json line carries the fixture transcript_path, and tests/unit/dashboard/server/services/agent-state-service.test.ts to assert a transcriptPath-carrying model_set event appends an entry with path.

items.title: Given a fixture SessionStart payload containing transcript_path, running session-start-hook produces a sessions.json line that contains that path.
Given the same payload, the emitted model_set event body contains transcriptPath with the same value.
Given a model_set event carrying transcriptPath, observeSessionIndexEvent appends a sessions.json entry that records that path.
Given jq is absent, the hook falls back to writing no new fields and still exits 0.
W3: Both resolver adapters prefer recorded paths over per-harness formulas

expected_outputs: Given an index entry carrying path whose file exists, then listAgentTranscriptCandidates returns that path as the entry's only candidate and resolves to it.
Given an entry without path, then resolution falls back to the per-harness formula exactly as before.
metadata.parallelSafeReason: Owns the two adapters and their two test files; writers append data the adapters only read.

narrative.Action: Make the identical edit in both entry loops — src/lib/agent-enrichment.ts listAgentTranscriptCandidatesSync (:263-284) and src/dashboard/server/routes/jsonl-resolver.ts listAgentTranscriptCandidates (:234-253): before the per-kind formula, `if (entry.path) { indexedPaths.set(transcriptCandidateKey(transcriptCandidateKind(entry.harness ?? currentHarness), entry.sessionId), entry.path); continue; }`. orderedTranscriptCandidates needs no change. Extend jsonl-resolver.test.ts with: path-carrying entry resolves to the recorded file with no formula-derived candidate for the same entry; missing recorded file falls through to the next older entry; pathless entry still resolves via its formula. Extend tests/lib/agent-enrichment-jsonl-identity.test.ts with the same fast-path coverage through getAgentJsonlPath using sessions.json fixtures whose entries carry path.

items.title: Given an entry with path, both adapters produce exactly one candidate for that entry and resolve to the recorded file when it exists.
Given a recorded path whose file is missing, resolution falls back to the next older entry's candidate.
Given an entry without path, the per-harness formula branch resolves it identically to before the change.
npx vitest run tests/lib/agent-enrichment-jsonl-identity.test.ts src/dashboard/server/routes/__tests__/jsonl-resolver.test.ts exits 0.

W6: Pi and ohmypi extensions record the session file at start and first turn end

expected_outputs: Given a session file matching *_<sessionId>.jsonl exists under the agent sessions dir at session_start, then the index entry records its path.
Given a turn_end event carrying sessionLogPath, then the extension appends an upgraded entry with that path exactly once.
metadata.parallelSafeReason: Two extension packages and their tests; disjoint from every other item.

narrative.Action: Apply the identical change to packages/pi-extension/src/index.ts and packages/ohmypi-extension/src/index.ts (maintained copies): appendSessionIndexEntry (pi :421-424 / ohmypi :428-431) gains an optional transcriptPath parameter spread into the serialized object when set (PIPE_BUF guard unchanged); handleSessionStart (pi :595-612 / ohmypi :616 region) scans join(paths.agentDir, 'sessions') recursively to depth 3, ignoring unreadable dirs, for a file named *_<sessionId>.jsonl or exactly <sessionId>.jsonl and passes the hit; handleTurnEnd, when event.sessionLogPath differs from a new module-level lastRecordedSessionPath, resolves the current id via sessionIdFor(env) (:390) and appends {sessionId, at, source: 'turn-end', harness: 'pi'|'ohmypi', model, path: sessionLogPath}, then updates lastRecordedSessionPath. Dedupe newest-wins makes the upgrade authoritative. Extend each package's src/__tests__/index.test.ts: session_start with a fixture file records path; session_start with no file records no path key; turn_end with sessionLogPath appends the upgrade once and a repeat appends nothing.

items.title: Given a fixture file <sessionsDir>/2026-09-20T10-00-00_<id>.jsonl exists, session_start records an entry containing that absolute path in both packages.
Given no matching session file at session_start, the appended entry contains no path key.
Given two turn_end events with the same sessionLogPath, exactly one upgraded entry is appended and parseSessionIndex preserves the path.

Given the production-only diff stat, then deletions meet or exceed insertions, or the shortfall is posted on the issue before pan done.
metadata.parallelSafeReason: Runs after w1 and w3 (shared files, edge-gated); it is the net-negative lever and the AC3 proof.
